nonBlockingIssues.description: behavioralContract array has no .min(1) constraint despite spec saying 'required, min 1'. Permissive for LLM output but deviates from spec.
EstimatedComplexitySchema is duplicated in plan-json-parser.ts and proto-step.ts. Should share from one canonical location.
fileReferences is optional in Zod schema but the spec says required. The spec itself is internally inconsistent (prose says required, code reference shows optional).
JSON example only shows one step. A multi-step example would better illustrate complex plans.
Curly-brace placeholders in file path could be confused with JSON syntax. Consider angle brackets.
options field is required in the prompt but optional in the canonical schema (json-plan-migration.md). Could cause workers to hallucinate options.
Minor wording ambiguity about 'overwrite at the same path' in consolidation prompt.
buildQuestionsSection() casts extra?.resolvedQuestions as types without runtime validation. Pre-existing pattern.
buildJsonPlanSteps silently returns empty array when parseJsonPlan fails — invalid JSON plan produces empty steps array.
Stale module comment in plan-confirmation-logic.ts still mentions 'legacy markdown plans'. PhaseSummaryItem type and phases field are vestigial.
Dispatcher always sees step index 0 and empty completedSteps — pre-existing limitation of JSON plan migration.
guardMutation() is advisory-only and not enforced at the queue mutation layer. Must be addressed during executor integration.
Single onStepCompleted hook limitation means sprint and quality gates hooks can't coexist without composition.
Title-based quality check detection ('feature quality check') is slightly brittle.
Executor doesn't wire guardrails into StepDispatchContext — mutation_budget is never populated in production.
applyMutations() doesn't auto-invoke checkConvergence() — callers must check separately.
MutationRequest.type is limited to insert_after/skip/remove — missing reorder and replace.
